description: Create coworking_spaces Supabase table schema, seed script, and hook. Then wire CoworkingSpaces.jsx and CoworkingDetail.jsx to prefer the new table.
steps: Create supabase/coworking_spaces_schema.sql following the pattern in supabase/job_openings_schema.sql. Table: coworking_spaces with columns: id UUID pk default gen_random_uuid(), name TEXT NOT NULL, city_slug TEXT NOT NULL, city_name TEXT, locality TEXT, state TEXT, full_address TEXT, pricing_hot_desk INTEGER, pricing_dedicated_desk INTEGER, pricing_private_cabin INTEGER, pricing_day_pass INTEGER, seats TEXT, rating NUMERIC, tags TEXT (pipe-separated), amenities TEXT (pipe-separated), featured_image TEXT, gallery TEXT (pipe-separated URLs), description TEXT, is_popular BOOLEAN DEFAULT false, is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true, sort_order INTEGER DEFAULT 0, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(), updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(). RLS enabled with public SELECT policy (anon can read where is_active=true). Index on (city_slug, is_active).

Create scripts/seed-coworking.mjs - an ES module script that: (a) connects to Supabase using the service key directly (hardcoded or from env SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY), (b) reads existing 75 spaces from the `spaces` table, (c) transforms each into a coworking_spaces row with varied pricing using a deterministic hash of the area name (hot desk: 55% of dedicated, private cabin: 170% of dedicated, day pass from dayMult logic, dedicated desk from deskMult logic matching the existing coworkingPriceMultiplier function), (d) uses upsert (on conflict id or name+city_slug) to insert into coworking_spaces. Include pipe-separated tags from property_feature, set city_slug using slugifySpace logic, set city_name from address_city, locality from address_area, state from address_state, featured_image, gallery from space_images (pipe-separated), seats as '4-100 seats'. The script should be runnable: node scripts/seed-coworking.mjs

Create src/hooks/useCoworkingSpaces.js following the pattern in src/hooks/useJobOpenings.js. It should fetch from the coworking_spaces table using the anon key (import supabase from src/lib/supabase.js), filter is_active=true, order by sort_order asc then rating desc, limit 500. Return { spaces: Array, loaded: boolean }.

Modify src/components/coworking/CoworkingSpaces.jsx: Import useCoworkingSpaces hook. When coworking_spaces data is loaded and non-empty, use it directly instead of transforming from useSupabaseSpaces(). Map coworking_spaces rows to card shape: {name, locality, price: pricing_dedicated_desk, dayPass: pricing_day_pass, seats, rating, tags: tags.split('|'), image: featured_image, popular: is_popular, citySlug: city_slug, cityName: city_name}. Keep the existing Supabase spaces transform as second fallback, and static data as third fallback.

Modify src/pages/CoworkingDetail.jsx: Import useCoworkingSpaces hook. Before trying static data or the spaces table fallback, look up the space from coworking_spaces by matching city_slug===city param and slugifyCoworking(name)===space param. When found, build the sp object using the direct pricing fields (pricing_dedicated_desk as price, pricing_day_pass as dayPass, pricing_hot_desk and pricing_private_cabin for the plans section). Use gallery field (split by |) for thumbnails, amenities field (split by |) for amenities list, description for the about text. Keep existing fallbacks intact.
acceptance_criteria: supabase/coworking_spaces_schema.sql exists with correct table definition, RLS policy, and index
scripts/seed-coworking.mjs runs successfully and populates coworking_spaces table from existing spaces data
src/hooks/useCoworkingSpaces.js exports a useCoworkingSpaces hook that fetches from coworking_spaces table
CoworkingSpaces.jsx prefers coworking_spaces data when available, falls back gracefully
CoworkingDetail.jsx looks up space from coworking_spaces first, uses pricing fields directly in plans section
verification: Run: export PATH="/root/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2/bin:$PATH" && cd /projects/sandbox/emo-websitenew && rm -rf dist && npm run build
findings: The Supabase REST API (PostgREST) cannot execute DDL statements. The coworking_spaces table must be created manually via the Supabase Dashboard SQL Editor (paste supabase/coworking_spaces_schema.sql). After table creation, run 'node scripts/seed-coworking.mjs' to populate. The seed script exits 0 in all cases and prints clear instructions when the table is missing. The build passes with all 398 pages. The hook and component wiring is complete - once the table exists and is seeded, the coworking pages will automatically prefer data from coworking_spaces over the old spaces table transform.
